'''Noah Clowney''' (born July 14, 2004) is an American professional [[basketball]] player for the [[Brooklyn Nets]] of the [[National Basketball Association]] (NBA). He played [[college basketball]] for the [[Alabama Crimson Tide men's basketball|Alabama Crimson Tide]].

==Early life and high school career==
Clowney grew up in [[Spartanburg, South Carolina]] and attended [[Dorman High School]].<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.tuscaloosanews.com/story/sports/college/basketball/2023/01/13/alabama-basketball-noah-clowney-nate-oats-lsu-tigers/69806647007/|title=Noah Clowney: Alabama basketball freshman on confidence ahead of LSU|work=[[Tuscaloosa News]]|date=January 13, 2023|access-date=January 23, 2023}}</ref> As a junior, he averaged 9.6 points, 7.9 rebounds, and 1.4 blocks per game over 26 games.<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.goupstate.com/story/sports/2021/11/01/alabama-basketball-signs-dorman-senior-noah-clowney/6233612001/|title=Alabama basketball lands Dorman senior Noah Clowney|work=[[Spartanburg Herald-Journal]]|date=November 1, 2021|access-date=February 10, 2023}}</ref> Clowney averaged 17.5 points, 9.7 rebounds, and 1.7 blocks per game during his senior season.<ref>{{cite web|url=https://alabama.rivals.com/news/i-was-always-overlooked-clowney-blossoms-in-first-season-with-alabama|title='I was always overlooked': Clowney blossoms in first season with Alabama|first=James|last=Benedetto|website=[[Rivals.com]]|date=December 21, 2022|access-date=January 23, 2023}}</ref>
 
Clowney was rated a four-star [[college recruiting|recruit]] and committed to playing college basketball for [[Alabama Crimson Tide men's basketball|Alabama]] over offers from [[Virginia Tech Hokies men's basketball|Virginia Tech]], [[Florida Gators men's basketball|Florida]], and [[Indiana Hoosiers men's basketball|Indiana]].<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.tuscaloosanews.com/story/sports/2021/11/01/alabama-basketball-noah-clowney/6241577001/|title=Alabama basketball lands commitment from 4-star forward Noah Clowney|work=[[Tuscaloosa News]]|date=November 1, 2021|access-date=January 23, 2023}}</ref>

==College career==

web|url=https://www.si.com/college/alabama/bamacentral/freshman-noah-clowney-looks-like-alabama-basketballs-hidden-gem|title=Freshman Noah Clowney Looks Like Alabama Basketball's Hidden Gem|first=Blake|last=Byler|website=[[SI.com]]|date=August 15, 2022|access-date=January 23, 2023}}</ref> In a game against the Chinese national team, he scored 11 points and grabbed 10 rebounds.<ref>{{cite web|url=https://247sports.com/college/alabama/Article/Alabama-Basketball-Freshman-Noah-Clowney-even-more-athletic-than-Crimson-Tide-initially-thought-196309744/|title=Freshman Noah Clowney even more athletic than Tide initially thought|first=Charlie|last=Potter|website=[[247Sports.com]]|date=October 29, 2022|access-date=February 10, 2023}}</ref> Clowney entered his freshman season as Alabama's starting power forward.<ref>{{cite web|url=https://247sports.com/Article/college-basketball-recruiting-nba-draft-noah-clowney-class-of-2022-204422730/|title=Alabama's Clowney continuing to ascend|first=Adam|last=Finkelstein|website=[[247Sports.com]]|date=February 8, 2023|access-date=February 10, 2023}}</ref> He was named the [[Southeastern Conference]] (SEC) Freshman of the Week for the first two weeks of December.<ref>{{cite web|url=https://247sports.com/college/alabama/Article/Alabama-Basketball-Noah-Clowney-named-SEC-Freshman-of-the-Week-for-second-week-in-a-row-200272738/|title=Noah Clowney named SEC Freshman of the Week for second week in a row|first=Charlie|last=Potter|website=[[247Sports.com]]|date=December 12, 2022|access-date=February 11, 2023}}</ref> Following the end of the season, Clowney entered the [[2023 NBA draft]].<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.tuscaloosanews.com/story/sports/college/basketball/2023/04/01/noah-clowney-nba-draft-2023-alabama-basketball/70061988007/|title=Alabama basketball's Noah Clowney declares for the NBA Draft|work=[[Tuscaloosa News]]|date=April 1, 2023|access-date=April 5, 2023}}</ref>

==Professional career==

=== Brooklyn Nets (2023–present) ===
====2023–24 season====
The [[Brooklyn Nets]] selected Clowney with the 21st overall pick in the [[2023 NBA draft]].<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.al.com/alabamabasketball/2023/06/noah-clowney-drafted.html|title=Noah Clowney drafted in first round of NBA draft by Brooklyn Nets|first=Michael|last=Casagrande|website=[[AL.com]]|date=June 22, 2023|access-date=June 23, 2023}}</ref> The Nets assigned Clowney to their [[NBA G League]] affiliate, the [[Long Island Nets]], on October 30, 2023.<ref name="NoahClowneyPlayerProfile">{{cite web|url=https://basketball.realgm.com/player/Noah-Clowney/Summary/162215|title=Noah Clowney Player Profile|website=RealGM|access-date=July 16, 2024}}</ref> His first G League action came on November 10, 2023, where he started in their Showcase Cup opener recording game-highs of 12 rebounds and 4 blocks, along with 12 points, in a 123–120 victory over [[Raptors 905]], despite fouling out in just 31 minutes.<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.al.com/sports/2023/11/noah-clowney-josh-primo-play-in-g-league-openers.html|title=Noah Clowney, Josh Primo play in G League openers|first=Mark|last=Inabinett|website=[[AL.com]]|date=November 11, 2023|access-date=July 16, 2024}}</ref><ref>{{cite web|url=https://basketball.realgm.com/gleague/boxscore/2023-11-10/Raptors-at-Raptors/449006|title=Box Score: Raptors 905 vs Long Island Nets (November 10, 2023)|website=RealGM|date=November 10, 2023|access-date=July 16, 2024}}</ref> He played in 15 games, all starts, during the Long Island Nets' 9-7 Showcase Cup campaign, averaging 13.1 points on 56.3% shooting, 8.5 rebounds, and 1.9 blocks per game.<ref name="NoahClowneyPlayerProfile"/><ref name="LongIslandSchedule">{{cite web|url=https://basketball.realgm.com/gleague/teams/Long-Island-Nets/46/Schedule/2024|title=Long Island Nets 2024 Schedule|website=RealGM|access-date=July 16, 2024}}</ref> 

Clowney would be recalled to the Nets and assigned back to Long Island numerous times throughout his first year.<ref name="NoahClowneyPlayerProfile" /> He got his first NBA action on November 25, 2023, grabbing one rebound in 3 minutes of play in a 112–97 win against the [[Miami Heat]]. On December 27, he checked in for his second NBA game, promptly scoring his first NBA points, 2 of the 14 he would put up in 24 minutes of action during a 124–144 loss to the [[Milwaukee Bucks]].<ref name="ClowneyGameLog">{{cite web|url=https://www.espn.com/nba/player/gamelog/_/id/4712896/noah-clowney|title=Noah Clowney Game Log|website=ESPN.com|access-date=July 16, 2024}}</ref><ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.nba.com/stats/events?CFID=&CFPARAMS=&GameEventID=189&GameID=0022300417&Season=2023-24&flag=1&title=Clowney%201%27%20Cutting%20Dunk%20Shot%20(2%20PTS)%20(Brooks%201%20AST)|title=Clowney 1' Cutting Dunk Shot (2 PTS) (Brooks 1 AST)|website=NBA.com|access-date=July 16, 2024}}</ref><ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.nba.com/game/mil-vs-bkn-0022300417/play-by-play?period=Q2|title=Milwaukee Bucks vs. Brooklyn Nets Play-by-Play (December 27, 2023)|website=NBA.com|access-date=July 16, 2024}}</ref> For the next couple months he would be recalled by Brooklyn and play in NBA games intermittently, still spending the bulk of his time with Long Island.<ref name="NoahClowneyPlayerProfile" /> In 19 games of the G-League regular season, he averaged an impressive 17.4 points in 30.6 minutes per game, to go along with 7.8 rebounds and 1.8 blocks per game, both team highs, helping Long Island to a 19–15 record and a playoff bid.<ref name="NoahClowneyPlayerProfile" /><ref name="LongIslandSchedule" /> 

On March 21, 2024, shortly before the G-League playoffs, he was again recalled to the Brooklyn Nets where he has remained since.<ref name="NoahClowneyPlayerProfile" /> He saw steady increases in appearances and minutes from this point through the end of the season and made the most of his opportunities.<ref name="ClowneyGameLog" /> On April 3, Clowney recorded 22 points, 10 rebounds and one assist off the bench in a 115–111 win against the [[Indiana Pacers]], going 7-for-9 from the field and 3-for-4 from three in just 17 minutes of playing time.<ref name="ClowneyGameLog" /><ref>{{Cite web |title=Noah Clowney Scores 22 {{!}} Highlights and Live Video from Bleacher Report |url=https://bleacherreport.com/videos/555926-noah-clowney-scores-22 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20240602155002/https://bleacherreport.com/videos/555926-noah-clowney-scores-22 |url-status=dead |archive-date=June 2, 2024 |access-date=2024-06-02 |work=Bleacher Report}}</ref> Despite the valiant effort, the win marked the Nets' elimination from playoff contention as the [[Atlanta Hawks]]' 121–113 win over the [[Detroit Pistons]] put the final [[NBA play-in tournament|Play-In Tournament]] spot out of reach.<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.espn.com/nba/recap/_/gameId/401585734|title=Nets vs. Pacers - Game Recap - April 3, 2024|website=ESPN.com|access-date=July 16, 2024}}</ref> With this came a marked increase for minutes for Clowney as [[Cameron Johnson|Cam Johnson]] and [[Dorian Finney-Smith]] shut it down for the season.<ref name="ClowneyGameLog" /> He started the final four games of the season for Brooklyn, the first of which (a 77–107 loss to the [[Sacramento Kings]]) was his first NBA start, where he recorded 7 points and 10 rebounds in 35 minutes.<ref name="ClowneyGameLog" />

====2024–25 season====
Clowney made 46 appearances (20 starts) for Brooklyn during the [[2024–25 NBA season]], averaging 9.1 points, 3.9 rebounds, and 0.9 assists. On April 2, 2025, Clowney was ruled out for the remainder of the season due to a right ankle sprain.<ref>{{cite web | last=Harris | first=Declan | title=Nets' Rising Star Reportedly Out For Season | website=Brooklyn Nets On SI | date=2025-04-04 | url=https://www.si.com/nba/nets/onsi/news/nets-rising-star-reportedly-out-for-season-noah-clowney | access-date=2025-12-06}}</ref>

====2025–26 season====
Clowney logged career-highs with 31 points and seven three-pointers in a losing effort against the [[2025–26 New York Knicks season|New York Knicks]] on November 24, 2025.<ref>{{Cite web |date=2025-11-25 |title=Knicks beat Nets 113-100 for 12th straight win over Brooklyn |url=https://apnews.com/article/knicks-nets-score-ef71607ec7ffa68e0cae40d4a3959039 |access-date=2025-11-25 |website=AP News |language=en}}</ref><ref>{{Cite web |date=2025-11-25 |title=Nets' Noah Clowney: Drops 31 points with seven treys |url=https://www.cbssports.com/fantasy/basketball/news/nets-noah-clowney-drops-31-points-with-seven-treys/ |access-date=2025-11-25 |website=CBS Sports |language=en}}</ref>
